en: Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling on Mount Potalaka, in the sanctuary of the Noble Avalokiteśvara, upon a divine lion-throne made of precious celestial gems and sapphire, strewn with flowers, together with a great community of monks numbering about five hundred—all of whom were arhats, whose taints were exhausted, who had attained mastery over their minds, and who had reached the further shore of the True Dharma—as well as with bodhisattvas. This is the Sūtra of the Array of the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas.

Accompanied by all those who have attained the wisdom of great compassion; by all those bound to only one more birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*); by two, three, ten, twenty, thirty, or even a hundred births;
by all those who have attained the eight fruits and abide on the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*), such as the noble Avalokiteśvara, Mañjuśrī, Vimalaketu, Ratnaśrī, Vajraketu, and Vimalaprabha.

Together with seven hundred bodhisattvas headed by Candana and Amṛtaketu; with all the laymen and laywomen who had received their predictions and attained meditative concentration; with five thousand gathered from various world-systems; with all hundreds of thousands of gandharvas who had served previous buddhas and witnessed the miracles of the Tathāgata; and together with all the great yakṣiṇīs.

He sat together with eighty great yakṣiṇīs headed by Anaupamya, Vimalaprabhā, Prabhāvatī, and the yakṣiṇī Bhīmaśrī— all of whom had attained the wisdom of a bodhisattva, received their prophecy, were irreversible,
and were non-comparable— along with these world-protectors: Śatakratu, Brahmā, Vaiśravaṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, Maṇibhadraputra, and Pūrṇabhadra.

Then, all of them, knowing that the Tathāgata was seated upon the lion throne, honored, worshiped, circumambulated hundreds of thousands of millions of times, and venerated him with their respective roots of merit— through divine ornaments, garments, flowers, garlands, incense, ointments, and the sound of music. At that time, the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption named "Abiding in the Wisdom of Great Compassion for All Sentient Beings."
By the power of that concentration and dhāraṇī, the trichiliocosm great thousandfold world-systems were illuminated by its radiance,
and all forms became clearly manifest.
Furthermore, those beings who were blind from birth saw forms with their eyes.
The deaf heard sounds with their ears;
those afflicted by disease became free from disease;
and the naked were clothed in garments.
The insane regained their mindfulness;
those with impaired bodies had their faculties restored to fullness;
and the poor obtained wealth.
Indeed, those beings who were previously deprived of wealth, goods, and enjoyments became endowed with wealth, goods, and enjoyments;
all beings were presented with every happiness and had all their aspirations fulfilled.
Whatever beings there were in the triple-thousand great thousandfold world-system, they approached the Blessed One with palms joined in reverence to hear the Dharma of instruction.

Those beings who had become gods, having abandoned all divine pleasures and practiced the recollection of the Buddha (*buddhānusmṛti*), approached the Blessed One where he was in order to hear the Dharma.
Those beings who had become humans likewise renounced human pleasures and approached the Blessed One where he was, desiring to hear the Dharma.

Those beings who had become *nāgas*, *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, *pretas*, *piśācas*, or *bhūtas*, having attained the recollection of the Buddha and developed a mind of loving-kindness (*maitracitta*) toward all sentient beings, obtained physical and mental happiness and [approached] to hear the Dharma.
They approached the place where the Blessed One was.
Those beings who were born in the world of Yama in blinding darkness also, through the power of the Buddha, attained mindfulness for a single moment and recognized one another;
they became completely liberated from that great darkness.
All sentient beings came to possess minds of mutual loving-kindness;
their secondary afflictions were exhausted.
At that very time, the great earth shook in six ways, rising and falling.
Then, while seated in that assembly, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara as follows:
"Noble son, in this great assembly that has been illuminated, the premonitory signs for the great assembly are perfectly clear;
and the prophecy for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Bodhisattvas has been revealed."
The preliminary sign of the Great Saying of the Dharma is now appearing.
Noble son, there will be the fulfillment of all aspirations and the attainment of great wisdom for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas.

Therefore, noble son, out of compassion for sentient beings, for their benefit and happiness, and for the sake of establishing them in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, you should question the Tathāgata.

"Noble son, in the future time, in the final age, there will be beings who are evildoers, impoverished, emaciated, with bodies of poor complexion, oppressed by old age and disease, possessing meager resources, with undeveloped bodies, short-lived, of little intelligence, and tormented by passion, hatred, and delusion. For their sake, noble son, entreat the Tathāgata to teach the Dharma; this will be for the long-term benefit, welfare, and happiness of sentient beings, and for the pacification of all diseases."

"For the warding off of all evils, for the pacification of all evils, for the fulfillment of all vows, and even unto the attainment of unsurpassed parinirvāṇa. Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, having looked toward the ten directions and brought to mind as many koṭis of Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, bowed with palms joined toward where the Blessed One was,
circumambulated him three times, prostrated with the five-pointed salutation, and addressed the Blessed One as follows:

“Blessed One, will there be beings in the future time who are oppressed by old age, sickness, sorrow, death, and the suffering of untimely death; who are emaciated, ill-favored, short-lived, possessed of meager resources, and whose bodies are undeveloped?

Will they, with hearts characterized by envy and immorality, kill one another and seize one another’s wealth, enjoyments, and power? Will they be devoted to laughter, dancing, acting, and play, perceiving the impermanent as permanent and the impure as pure?”
With that as their cause and that as their basis, those beings will be reborn in various forms among the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama.

Therefore, O Blessed One, for their sake, for their welfare, for the fulfillment of all their hopes, up to the point of bringing about the wisdom of a Tathāgata, for their birth in a Buddha-field, and for the warding off of all evil, speak, O Blessed One; speak, O Sugata! There is no such thing as knowledge belonging to a Tathāgata that is unknown, unseen, unheard, or even unperceived.

“Blessed One, many bodhisattvas, monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, kinnaras, and others have assembled, desiring to hear this discourse on the Dharma; they have attended upon previous Buddhas and have become endowed with wisdom. Yet, having become devoid of hope, they will depart.
Then that entire assembly, having gathered there, prostrated with the five-fold salutation and spoke with one voice:
“Excellent, Blessed One! Please speak, Blessed One! Please speak, Sugata!

Then the Blessed One, having recognized this request for a second and even a third time, looked toward the ten directions and, with a voice that was beautiful and charming, addressed the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara:

“Noble son, there is a samādhi called ‘The Array of Manifesting Buddha-fields while Beholding Sentient Beings through the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas,’ which was heard by me in the past, beginning from my first generation of the mind of awakening.”
It was heard from the presence of the Tathāgata Sukusumajyotiḥsandarśana;
and upon merely hearing the name of that samādhi, ninety koṭis of beings attained the wisdom of a Tathāgata,
and they were all prophesied by the Tathāgatas for various buddha-fields.
And I, noble son, have attained the prophecy.
I remember, noble son, through the divine knowledge of a Tathāgata, that this Dharma discourse was spoken for the benefit of sentient beings by thirty thousand Tathāgatas;
in every instance, it was you, Noble Avalokiteśvara, and Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta who requested the Tathāgatas [to teach it].
And when this assembly of all the bodhisattvas who had gathered— along with the assemblies of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen— heard this, they all paid it honor and made offerings.
Thereupon, many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sentient beings received prophecies and became attainers of the bodhisattva samādhis.

They attained all their desires; having fulfilled all their hopes, they flourished, became free from disease, and reached full maturity in their roots of merit. Having abandoned all obscurations, they were handsome, gracious, and beautiful to behold; they were enriched with wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses. They were highly esteemed by all kings, princes, and ministers, and were worthy of veneration by all sentient beings. Endowed with mindfulness and wisdom, they possessed unshakable faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha. Steadfast, they were endowed with longevity, beauty, splendor, strength, and vigor, being possessed of the excellence of every supreme form.
And never shall there be separation from what is dear, nor shall there be any calamity involving what is dear.
In this way, noble son, those sons of good family or daughters of good family will be endowed with many virtues.

Whenever they prostrate with the five limbs toward this discourse on the true Dharma, having adorned it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, umbrellas, banners, and flags, and having said "Homage to the Buddha," they shall pay their respects.

They will give their approval, uphold it, recite it, cause it to be recited, write it down, and cause it to be written down; having generated a mind of supreme reverence toward that Dharma-preacher, they will in this very life be endowed with all excellent qualities: they will be handsome, pleasing, beautiful to behold, free from disease, long-lived, steadfast in intellect, and possessed of mindfulness.
Possessing fortitude, they will be objects of admiration, worthy of salutation, and worthy of honor by all kings, queens, princes, ministers, all enemies, and all sentient beings.
They will possess abundant wealth and requisites,
and the fragrance of sandalwood will emanate from their mouths.
His eyes will be like blue lotuses;
day and night he will behold Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
and all his obscurations, including the five deeds of immediate retribution and so forth, will be exhausted.
The deities will protect him;
at the time of death, he will have a vision of the Buddha and a vision of the Bodhisattvas;
and he will not die with a mind full of envy or a distracted mind.
Until they pass away and are reborn in the world-system of Sukhāvatī, O son of good family, I have granted them a face-to-face prophecy.
They have seen me and have honored and revered me;
they should not give rise to any doubt.

Those who, for the sake of awakening, shall uphold this Dharma-discourse, and who honor it, write it, cause it to be written, recite it, worship it, master it, and hear its name— thinking "this is a bodhisattva," they should be honored.

Whatever deficiencies in form, deficiencies in wealth, deficiencies in intelligence, or whatever verbal abuse, separation from loved ones, and disturbances of sovereignty he may have experienced through the ripening of past karma— all these shall [be overcome] by the power of this samādhi.

Some through hearing [the teaching], some through headache, some through the interruption of food, some through wearing ragged clothing, some through affliction of body and mind, some through lying on a bed of painful contact, and some through being rebuked—all that karmic obscuration shall go to destruction.

And he should generate this thought: "In the past, while wandering in saṃsāra, I accumulated various kinds of evil and unwholesome deeds toward sentient beings; I confess them and reveal them, and I do not [conceal them]."
I shall conceal it.
One should generate a mind of unbreakable faith toward the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.

And whatever karmic obstruction there may be for that son of good family or daughter of good family which would result in the fruit of the destruction of enjoyments—whether toward the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, or toward the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas—[one should conceal it].
Or whatever evil karma may have been committed or accumulated by their mother or father, all of that will go to complete exhaustion.
They will become endowed with great sovereignty and prosperity.

Furthermore, whatever karmic obstruction there may be for that son of good family or daughter of good family which is to be experienced as suffering in hell, which leads to separation from loved ones, or which leads to being blind from birth—[all such things shall be purified].

Whatever karma leading to rebirth as a woman, whatever leads to the appearance of both sexual organs, and whatever leads to the realm of Yama, the world of hungry ghosts, or the animal realm through the power of envy, pride, and anger—all that shall be completely exhausted.
Thus, noble son, this samādhi is a mine of all virtues.
Noble son, there are those who will ensure that this Dharma discourse remains for a long time.
And for those sons of good family and daughters of good family, they provide protection, defense, and guardianship;

they fulfill all virtues and all aspirations; they bring about great wealth, sovereignty, and happiness; they cause the fulfillment of every thought and prayer; they exhaust all karma; they pacify all untimely death, bad dreams, and all diseases; they ensure victory in all battles; they bestow long life, beauty, strength, vigor, and stability; they bring all yakṣas, bhūtas, and humans under one's control; they pacify all fevers, poisons, and afflictions; and they lead up to the attainment of the prophecy of enlightenment.

Those sons of good family or daughters of good family who, having heard these dhāraṇī mantra-words, have retained them, recited them, honored them, written them down, or caused them to be written down for the sake of protection— they all obtain these very qualities. Then, at that time, this great earth shook in six ways.
And that assembled multitude, having covered the Tathāgata with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, and pairs of fine garments, gave their applause, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Blessed One! What are those mantra-words?
Homage to all the Tathāgatas! Namely: *buddhe subuddhe śuddhamate*."

O you who look upon the world and look beyond the world; O you who observe sentient beings, empowered by the empowerment of all Tathāgatas; O you who fulfill all aspirations, bearer of radiant light, honored even in the hells, giver of Tathāgata-knowledge, and established through the empowerment of the Tathāgata!
May all the world be happy.
May past karma be exhausted. This is [the donation] of me, the great lay devotee (upāsaka) Śulivajra, a disciple of the venerable Mārapati Śukṣiṇa.
May there be protection from all fears through the empowerment of the Tathāgata; svāhā!

Noble sons, these mantra-words have been spoken and empowered by thirty thousand Tathāgatas; they are now likewise spoken by me for the sake, benefit, and happiness of all sentient beings, for their protection, defense, and concealment, as bringers of the pacification of all diseases, and for rebirth in a Buddha-field. Whoever in this assembly should know thus: "How indeed may we obtain all these virtues spoken by the Tathāgatas?"—by that person, having risen early in the morning with a heart of compassion for all sentient beings...

With a mind of compassion, a mind of loving-kindness, free from envy, pride, hypocrisy, and anger, and with a one-pointed mind, having performed a most magnificent worship of the Buddha and paid homage to all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, one should bring the qualities [of the Buddha] to mind as desired, recite the mantra one hundred and eight times, and offer a single flower to each Tathāgata. Thereupon, all of that person's aspirations will be fulfilled.
Furthermore, one will behold the Tathāgata in dreams and shall obtain whatever boon one desires. At the time of death as well, one will behold the Tathāgata.
Having passed away, he will be reborn in the world-realm of Sukhāvatī,
endowed with long life, strength, complexion, and vigor;
and all his enemies will come under his control.
Furthermore, while this dhāraṇī was being spoken, sixty thousand living beings attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
All of them became liberated from all karmic obstructions and their every aspiration was fulfilled.
Then, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having surveyed the ten directions, addressed the Blessed One as follows:

“Blessed One, there exists a dhāraṇī for bodhisattvas called ‘Fearless Splendor,’ which I received from the presence of the Tathāgata Abhayavyūharāja. Having received it, I have proclaimed it to all sentient beings. Furthermore, Blessed One, I do not know of anyone—even in a dream—in whose ear-cavity that dhāraṇī has fallen and entered, who would experience weakness, affliction, or disease in their body.”

Whether it be fever, bodily pain, mental affliction, or untimely death; whether water, weapons, poison, or artificial venom; whether a *ḍākinī*, a spirit (*bhūta*), a *yakṣa*, enemies, or humans or non-humans—there is no possibility that they could cause harm or inflict injury.
Therefore, may the Blessed One grant permission for me to bestow the seal of the Bodhisattva’s vow.

For the sake of those Dharma-preachers, those who listen to the Dharma, those who hear it, those who honor it, those who worship it, those who uphold it, and those who recite it—[these mantras] fulfill all aspirations. Homage to all Buddhas! Homage to all Bodhisattvas and Arhats!
Namely: Oṃ vajradhara vajradhara vajrakāya vajrabala vajrateja | hūṃ hūṃ | Vajrapāṇi, protect the command of the Tathāgata!
Remember your vow!
Destroy all diseases and all evils!
Grant me the boon as I desire. To me!
“O Mārapati, do not obstruct the auspicious arrival of Śūlivajra!
Whatever we pray for, may that very thing be fulfilled!
He he!”
Turu turu! Come, come!
Do not delay!
Reveal the vajra-body! Reveal the vajra-body!
By the empowerment of the Buddha, svāhā!
While this dhāraṇī is being recited, let this great earth rise up and sink down.

All the yakṣas and rākṣasas were agitated, and all the gods, as well as humans and non-humans, were filled with wonder and cried out, "Excellent! Excellent! "Well said, well said, Great Beings! These dhāraṇī mantra-words have been spoken as supreme accomplishments. Then the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Blessed One in this way:

"Venerable Blessed One, whoever desires the stage of a bodhisattva, or wealth, grain, enjoyments, sovereignty, kingship, the state of a vidyādhara, or long life, strength, vigor, and longevity— by that person,
on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, a Vajradhara made of white sandalwood should be fashioned, laughing loudly (Aṭṭahāsa) and adorned with all ornaments;
it should be made with a heart containing relics."

One should perform [the rite] with a Vajradhara image containing the relics, which provides consolation and is held by a Vidyādhara, while incense is being burned; this must be done by one who is pure and has fasted for a day and night.

Then, on the eighth day, having performed the preliminary consecration (pūrva-seka) and having made great offerings of incense, flowers, perfumes, and lamps in a pure place where a Tathāgata resides, one should recite the mantra eight hundred times three times over [the image], and worship should be performed for the Tathāgata.

Having paid homage to all the Tathāgatas, having placed four full vases, having prepared a maṇḍala made of red sandalwood, and being clothed in white garments with a one-pointed mind, one should offer oblations of meat, perfumes, wine, and milk-rice in the four directions; then, with eight hundred *sumana* flowers, Vajrapāṇi should be invoked.
Until the fifteenth day, thereafter there will be a great sound, an earthquake, and rays of light will issue forth.
Then I shall grant whatever boon is desired.
All actions and all undertakings will be accomplished by the mere recitation [of this mantra].
One will be free from disease, long-lived, and liberated from all evils.
He shall obtain a thousand virtues;
at the time of death he shall see a Buddha,
and I too shall grant him my vision.
Then the Blessed One gave his approval, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Vajrapāṇi! This mudrā is not to be transgressed;
no doubt, no uncertainty, and no hesitation should be entertained toward it by the world including the gods. III
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta said this to the Blessed One:
"For what reason, Blessed One, is this samādhi called 'The Array of the Manifestation of Buddha-fields through the Observation of Beings by the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas'?
The Blessed One replied:
Through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas and being empowered by all Bodhisattvas, he attains all samādhis and the gateways of all dhāraṇīs.
He discerns the mental states and mental factors, as well as the contractions and expansions [of mind], of all sentient beings.

He knows that among gods, nāgas, humans, yakṣas, gandharvas, pretas, those born in the animal realm, and those in the world of Yama, these beings have approached merit and performed good deeds toward the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.
They attain clarity of faith.
To those beings who go to hell, who follow evil deeds, and who commit sinful acts— those who have fallen into wrong views— he teaches the Dharma and restrains them from all evils.
He establishes them in the awakening of a Buddha and fulfills all their aspirations.
He dispels envy, pride, anger, and avarice.
And those beings, having attained serene confidence in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, are reborn in the Buddha-fields.
They never experience suffering or mental distress.
Therefore, noble son, this is called the samādhi named "The Array of Manifesting Buddha-fields while Beholding Sentient Beings through the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas.
Having heard it, they attain the stage of certainty and non-retrogression.
He asked: "In what sense, Blessed One, do those sons of good family receive their prediction?
What is the magnitude of their mass of merit? And what is their difficult practice?"
“Blessed One, it is difficult to attain even arhatship, let alone unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

The Blessed One said, “Noble son, consider both that which I have fulfilled—the perfections of generosity, ethical discipline, patience, vigor, meditative concentration, and wisdom—beginning from my first production of the thought of awakening; and that which was the relinquishing of my head, hands, feet, eyes, limbs, dear sons, wife, daughters, male servants, and female servants.”

The accumulation of merit consisting in the honoring, reverencing, copying, causing to be copied, reciting, and memorizing this Dharma-discourse, as well as the accumulation of merit consisting in its proclamation to others and the accumulation of merit consisting in the honoring and reverencing of those Dharma-preachers—this former accumulation of merit does not approach even a hundredth part of that [latter] accumulation of merit. Furthermore, O son of good family, whatever Dharma has been spoken and mastered by me, all of that one should honor, revere, esteem, and worship; having honored it, one should copy it or cause it to be copied.
Whoever writes, recites, honors, or elucidates this Dharma-discourse will acquire a far greater accumulation of merit than this;
therefore, the Tathāgata prophesies their attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Why is that?
It is difficult to hear, take up, retain, honor, or write down a Dharma discourse of such a nature.

And those beings, who are of evil conduct, delighting in food, drink, laughter, and dance; who perceive the impure as pure; who abound in lust, anger, and malice; and who perceive what is not happiness as happiness; who delight in striking, reviling, threatening, and beating—they will neither understand nor take it to heart.

Then, due to that ignorance which is the cause of their evil karma, and being taken hold of by unwholesome friends, they are tormented by old age, sickness, grief, and death; at the time of death, they are filled with despair.
Seeing one another hanging from a couch resembling a cemetery, they will neither produce a wholesome state of mind nor an indestructible faith.
Having passed away from there, they will once again experience sufferings.

"Noble son, those who have not cultivated roots of merit, who have not beheld the Tathāgata, and who have not received the prediction [of enlightenment], are unable to hear, honor, worship, or take up this [teaching]; they cannot write it, cause it to be written, believe in it, nor can they revere, honor, or worship those Dharma-preachers.
Noble son, wherever this Dharma-discourse circulates, there the work of the Tathāgata will be accomplished."
Then that assembled multitude, having gathered together, gave their approval, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Blessed One!

We too, Blessed One, shall honor, revere, and respect the Dharma-preacher and the listener of the Dharma as if they were the Tathāgata himself, and we shall provide for them all the requisites for comfort."
"And we shall cause this Dharma-discourse to be widely propagated and we shall protect it, so that this Dharma-discourse will endure for a long time.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One, having looked upon the assembly gathered there, spoke thus:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son!"
"Alas! You must act even in this way:

becoming indifferent to body and mind, you must cause this Dharma-discourse to be heard, written down, and recited, even when subjected to all manner of disturbances, contempt, abuse, threats, blows, and insults."

And that Dharma-preacher and Dharma-listener should be attended with every provision for comfort. That region, that island, and that city should be protected from all fears, calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions.
And one should constantly and continuously keep that son of good family or daughter of good family in mind.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"Listen, son of good family, with heedfulness; do not be regretful in the future."
The arising of a Buddha is obtained only once in hundreds of thousands of millions of eons.
If one hears these qualities and places faith in them,
it will not be difficult for such a person to attain meditative concentration for as many millions of eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges.
Whoever should give a gift to those who are the best among bipeds.
Wealth, grain, as well as clothing and ornaments,
perfumes, garlands, and ointments— whosoever, having placed their faith in this sūtra, [bestows these].
Whoever should hear it, recite it, or cause it to be written down— for that merit no measure exists;
and that [merit] has been taught by the Sugata to be immeasurable.
One should always resort to the forest with constant vigilance,
and one should always meditate on meditation with a focused mind; and one should give gifts even of one's beloved sons and daughters.
One should renounce both hands and feet.
If someone were to uphold this sutra, they would obtain a distinction of merit even greater than that;
for one who gives the meaning of this excellent sutra is a true donor.
All states of woe are forever avoided by him.
For one who is indeed a giver of wealth and grain,
all virtues are not difficult to attain;
neither longevity, strength, nor vigor is hard for him to obtain.
Whoever upholds this pure sūtra.
They shall behold the Buddha Amitābha, the Leader;
he too has been prophesied by me for the awakening of a Buddha.
Not even a trace of evil shall ever exist in him.
He will behold the world-system Sukhāvatī.
Whatever karma he may have,
it will all be exhausted within the nest of his mind; likewise, there shall be no pain in the body nor fever in the head.
He shall never suffer a downfall;
moreover, he shall obtain visible qualities,
and everything that was thought of and prayed for.
Therefore, those monks, nuns,
laymen, laywomen, and kings should always show profound respect and honor toward the Dharma-preacher.
As it is for the Lord of Men, so it is for the Tathāgata.
And this sutra should always be upheld, and one should always show honor to its upholder with perfumes, garlands, and ointments.
And having shown honor, one should have it written down.
Do not, in a future time, wander through the hells and among the animals, afflicted by old age and disease and distracted by many thousands of miseries.
They will be born as eunuchs and impotent men, objects of loathing;
blind from birth, like corpses with a foul stench, they will be conceived in the wombs of women from lowly families.
For one who is envious, always acting wickedly, overcome by anger, and possessive,
even after having shown reverence toward the Buddhas and their teachings—
He will be reborn among these very classes of beings;
experiencing sufferings right there, do not let yourselves be tormented in the future.
Therefore, he who always honors those [teachings], and whoever should uphold and proclaim them—
even if others should subject him to abuse— [is the one truly honored].
Contempt, as well as beating and binding.
By that [act], he has indeed reviled me, yet having shown honor to me, he honors the upholder;
therefore, they should always [show respect] toward the Dharma-preacher.
Whoever should uphold, write down, or recite it, they should always show honor and perform acts of service; and they should speak words that are affectionate and sweet. IV.
The Bodhisattva Āryāvalokiteśvara, having prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One as follows:

"I remember, Blessed One, a dhāraṇī called the *Vyavalokanaprātihāryā*, which was previously received and heard by me in the presence of the Tathāgata Jñānaketuprabhākara; having heard it, reflected upon it, received it, retained it, recited it, honored it, written it down, and caused it to be written down, beings attain the stage of non-retrogression."
They shall attain all these qualities spoken by the Tathāgata;
everything shall be fulfilled for them according to their aspirations,
and all their karmic obscurations shall go to exhaustion.
One attains meditative concentration; ailments are dispelled;
and there is the vision of the Buddhas and the vision of the Bodhisattvas.
Then the Blessed One gave his approval, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son! You have been empowered by the Tathāgata; proceed.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara, having paid homage to all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, spoke these mantra words:
Homage to all the Tathāgatas, who fulfill all aspirations! Homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Greatly Compassionate One! It is as follows:
*ha ha ha ha*, *mama mama*.
Dhīri dhīri!
O you who are peaceful, perfectly tranquil, and the destroyer of all evils;
look upon me, O Compassionate One, and bring the thought of awakening (bodhicitta) to mind.
Look upon me; remember, remember that true-word empowerment (satyādhiṣṭhāna) which was previously performed by you!
By that truth, fulfill all my hopes!
Purify the buddha-field!
May no one cause me harm!
By the empowerment of the Buddha, svāhā! It is thus:
Teje teje mahāteje!
Whatever bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, or mental misconduct I have committed, or whatever poverty I have suffered—may you extinguish that for me! Behold me! Look upon me!
For I long to behold the Tathāgata and to behold the Bodhisattvas.
Dhudhupa! Grant me your vision!
May all my virtues increase! Homage to all the Tathāgatas!
Homage to Avalokiteśvara!
Remember your vow, O Great Beings!
May the words of the mantra be accomplished! Svāhā!
While this dhāraṇī was being spoken, a great earthquake occurred and a great sound of joyful acclaim arose.
A rain of divine flowers fell, and the entire assembly exclaimed, "Excellent!
Excellent! saying, "Well-spoken is this by the Mahāsattva; it is for the protection of all beings and fulfills all hopes."
"Protect us from all fears, O destroyer of all karma, pacifier of death, evil dreams, and the wilderness!
We too, having become [your followers], shall uphold and honor you.
Avalokiteśvara said:
Whosoever, noble son, desires these qualities;
whoever desires the prophecy as proclaimed by the Tathāgata for me;

whoever desires the direct vision of me, the attainment of samādhi, the vision of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, the attainment of wealth and sovereignty, and rebirth in a Buddha-field—by him, during the bright fortnight, being pure and with limbs well-washed...

Having observed the noble eightfold fast, beginning on the eighth day, one should worship that spot of earth—which is empowered by the Buddha—in a clean location with perfumes, flowers, banners, flags, and full water-jars.

Then, having bathed his body thoroughly, being pure and clad in white garments, that Dharma-preacher should be worshipped with various flowers, garlands, and scents; and [the scripture] should be caused to be written down for the sake of roots of merit not shared with all other beings.

Having cultivated a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings, a mind of compassion, and a mind of pity, and having established a mind of profound reverence for the Tathāgata, one should write it day by day, beginning from the eighth day until the fifteenth, writing for half a day each day while performing that same ritual worship.
Then, by the mere act of writing according to this very procedure, his five deeds of immediate retribution and all his misdeeds will go to destruction.
He will increase in wholesome qualities;
he will possess ardent vigor;
and he will attain physical ease regarding all phenomena.
Attachment, aversion, delusion, pride, and anger will become attenuated.

Therefore, having had [this] written down, one should place an image of the Tathāgata facing eastward together with relics, as well as an image of Avalokiteśvara together with relics; and in that shrine containing the relics, a most magnificent worship should be performed with flowers, incense, perfumes, and lamps.
Starting from the eighth day until the fifteenth, one should maintain a mind of great compassion for all sentient beings.

Eating pure, white food, observing the noble eightfold fast (*āryāṣṭāṅga-upavāsa*), accompanied by virtuous friends, and completely free from pride, anger, and envy, one should perform increasingly magnificent worship day by day and recite the mantra eight hundred times during the three periods of the day.
Having offered lamps, incense, flowers, perfumes, and so forth, one should worship the image of Noble Avalokiteśvara with eight hundred *sumana* flowers during the three periods of the day.
Incense should also be offered to Vajrapāṇi.

Having paid homage to the ten directions, an offering of various flavors, drinks, curd-rice, and boiled rice should be cast in the four directions: to the goddess Bhīmā in the west, to Anopamā in the east, and to Śaṅkhinī above.
Consequently, no one will cause him distraction;
neither will fear arise,
nor will there be any alteration of his mind.
For all [of these], there is a recitation of one hundred and eight times, and an invocation with one hundred and eight *sumana* flowers.

Having performed the preliminary sprinkling according to this very procedure, then on the full moon of the fifteenth day, having set out four full jars, having offered incense, sandalwood, *kunduruka*, and camphor, and having provided four lamps,

having adorned that site of earth with various perfumes, banners, cloth streamers, and vessels of gold and silver, [one should offer] curds, honey, milk-rice, rice mixed with curds, and other offerings as they may be obtained.
Having offered [the mantra] in the four directions and presented eight hundred jasmine flowers (*sumanaḥpuṣpa*), one should recite it once for each flower and cast them in the four directions.
As before, having recited it once for each of two hundred and sixty-four jasmine and *jāti* flowers, one should fetch an image of the noble Avalokiteśvara.
Then, that authentic image will tremble.
A great roar will arise;
rays of light will issue forth;
and an earthquake will occur.
Then all his actions and all his undertakings will prosper;
he will behold the Tathāgata, attain the stages of a Bodhisattva, and become worthy of homage by all sentient beings.
He will be enriched with wealth, grain, treasuries, and granaries; he will be free from all diseases and long-lived.
All enemies will desire to see all kings, princes, and ministers; they will become well-wishers, having abandoned all afflictions, passion, hatred, and delusion.
There shall never be any separation from what is dear.

Endowed with great, firm strength and vigor, radiant, possessing sharp faculties, wise, with a heart of compassion for all beings, and knowing the Dharma, until the time of his passing, [he shall behold] the Buddha, the Blessed One, and the Noble Avalokiteśvara.
He sees that one who dwells in loving-kindness passes away;
while teaching the Dharma, he is reborn in whichever Buddha-fields or families of great universal monarchs he so desires, wherever he directs his mindfulness.

And he shall obtain many thousands of other virtues as well. Thus, Blessed One, this Dharma-discourse produces manifold qualities. These dhāraṇī-mantra words of yours cannot be heard, nor retained, nor honored, nor written, nor caused to be written, without the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of the Tathāgata.
One will not have faith.
If there is seeing, there will be no hearing;
if there is hearing, one will listen with a distracted mind, and thus will not have faith and will not show respect.
If one honors [this] with a mind of affliction and malice, or if one writes it or causes it to be written with a distracted mind—
[for what reason?]—
it is because, due to the cause of the fruit of former evil karma, that karma must be experienced.
He will fall into doubt;
he will commit one of the five deeds of immediate retribution.
Through three means of accomplishment, all his aspirations will be fulfilled.
No doubt, no uncertainty, and no hesitation should be conceived here.
Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son!"
This Dharma discourse shall perform the work of a Tathāgata for all sentient beings. Then the great yakṣiṇī Anopamā approached the Blessed One;
having covered the Blessed One with pairs of various flowered garments and prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One, she addressed the Blessed One as follows:
Thus do I remember, Blessed One: while the Blessed One was dwelling in Kauśāmbī in the Ghoṣila Grove, I made a vow before him for the sake of all sentient beings.
"Blessed One, I too know the heart-essence (*hṛdaya*) of all the vidyādharas.
May the Blessed One grant me permission for this, for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, and for the fulfillment of all hopes of the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen."
Homage to all Tathāgatas! Namely: ha ha | hī hī | hu hu |
Move on! Move on! Quickly, quickly! Swiftly, swiftly!
O Great Vidyā, honored by all holders of vidyās!
Hasaḥ hasaḥ! Why do you stand? Why do you stand?
O you whose limbs are adorned with ornaments variegated with gold, *paṭa paṭa*!
*bhara bhara*!
*bhiri bhiri*!
Bhūru bhūru!
Accomplish all my aims!
Turu turu!
Accomplish the goal!
Give me the wealth;
I cannot endure the lordship of Māra over one who is destitute.
Success for all the Saṅghas! Hā hā!
Padme padme mahāpadme!
Viśade viśade mahāviśade!
Bhava, Bhava, for the arising from existence!
To him, the Terrible; to him, the Terrible!
Teach me that knowledge!
Grant success!
Fulfill all my aims through the empowerment of the Buddhas, svāhā!

Whoever seeks the qualities of the Blessed One, seeks wealth and grain, seeks to bring all sentient beings under their influence, or desires great sovereignty, kingship, or the state of a Vidyādhara—may they also behold me face to face.

On the eighth day of the bright fortnight, on a new cloth with uncut fringes and free of hair, a pure painter—having observed the noble eight-limbed fast—should paint it using unmixed pigments contained in nine vessels.

In the center, an image of the Tathāgata should be depicted teaching the Dharma; to the right, the noble Vajrakrodha, brandishing a vajra, adorned with all ornaments and wearing flower garlands and half-moon necklaces.

On the left side is Anopamā, clothed in white garments, as fair as a stalk of reed, adorned with all ornaments, wearing white robes, holding a lotus in her hand, and offering consolation. Then, a pure Vidyādhara, having observed the noble eightfold fast, subsisting on milk and barley gruel, dressed in white garments, accompanied by a second person, and having performed the preliminary sprinkling on the eighth day at a pure site containing relics of the Tathāgata,
should perform worship with various flowers, perfumes, incense, and lamps, and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times three over.

Reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times for each individual *sumana* flower, that image of the Tathāgata and Vajrapāṇi should be brought forth; first, flowers, incense, and perfumes should be offered.
An oblation (*bali*) consisting of rice gruel with curd, various flavors, and various intoxicants should be cast in the four directions.

On the full moon of the fifteenth day, the oblation should be offered according to this very procedure, and other offerings such as incense, camphor, *kunduruka*, sandalwood, and ointments should be given as they are available.
Two lamps should be offered with fragrant oil;

there I shall appear in my own form and grant whatever boon is desired: the attainment of meditative concentration, the power of traveling through the sky, invisibility, kingship, the status of a powerful universal monarch (*cakravartin*), the state of a knowledge-holder (*vidyādhara*), the science of treasure-finding, the science of alchemy, or the knowledge of others' thoughts.
Longevity;
one should maintain a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings;
and one should be free from pride, anger, envy, and avarice, and refrain from misappropriating the property of stūpas, the Dharma, or the Saṅgha.

One should possess unshakable faith in the Tathāgatas. Blessed One, if I were to commit the five deeds of immediate retribution and You did not attend to me with these three means, and if, Blessed One, I were not to awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—

should anyone lack faith in the Buddha, or fall into doubt, or having committed evil and unwholesome deeds, fail to adopt restraint, and possess a mind of afflictions and secondary afflictions— even for such a person, may I grant my vision.
"I shall give you a gift and I shall also provide for your profit. Then the Blessed One gave his approval: "Excellent, excellent, sister!"
Excellent indeed, sister, that for the sake of all sentient beings you have spoken these such mantra-words and made this vow toward sentient beings of evil conduct.
By means of such great compassion as this, you will be able to establish all sentient beings in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
in this very way, it must also be done by you.
Then the Great Goddess Śaṅkhinī, having worshipped the Blessed One with various flowers and various perfumes, circumambulated him, prostrated at his feet, and addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"I too, Blessed One, through the empowerment of the Tathāgata, shall make a vow for the sake of the long endurance of the Tathāgata’s teaching.
And for those preachers of the Dharma and listeners of the Dharma, I shall provide mantra-words that fulfill all their aspirations."
May the Blessed One grant me permission for this protection.
Homage, homage to all the Tathāgatas!
Oṃ, Goddess Śaṅkhinī, come, come!
Stay, O Dhanajayā!
Vṛ vṛ vṛ, O increaser of prosperity!
Dhṛ dhṛ dhṛ, O bestower of steadfastness!
O you who bear various and manifold garments, ornaments, and weapons!
Yū yū, O protectress of life!
Remember the Tathāgatas and the thought of awakening; do not delay!
"Grant me a boon!
Śaṅkhini svāhā!
By these mantra-words, that Blessed One, having them present within his body, will attain an increase in glory.
He shall attain an increase of splendor, an increase of enjoyments, an increase of sovereignty, long life, and the power to subjugate enemies.

Having offered a bali-oblation with whatever is available that has been consecrated by one hundred and eight recitations, one should perform a most magnificent worship of the Tathāgata with incense and *kunduruka* in the four directions;
a lamp should also be offered.
For twenty-one days, one must abide in loving-kindness and remain established in the observance.
Then, with the exception of those who reject the true Dharma, I shall fulfill all their intentions.
This should be performed in a clean place or in a temple of the gods.
Then the Blessed One and the assembled assembly gave their approval, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, sister! This is well-spoken."
The vow is endowed with many virtues;
in the same way, you too must act thus in the future time.
Then, indeed, the Great Queen Bhīmā, having honored the Blessed One with golden flowers and prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One as follows:

I too, Blessed One, for the sake of those Dharma-preachers, those listeners of the Dharma, those scribes, those retainers, those reciters, and those worshippers, shall provide mantra-words that fulfill all hopes,
which bestow gold, jewels, pearls, enjoyments, sovereignty, kingship, and long life, and which subjugate enemies.
Whosoever— whether a king or queen, or a monk, nun, layman, or laywoman— shall uphold, honor, write, or cause to be written [this], with devotion and the profound respect due to a Tathāgata;

Blessed One, I shall protect those who practice according to what has been taught, I shall provide them with full guardianship, I shall grant them appropriate boons, and I shall ensure they lack nothing in terms of enjoyments and sovereignty.
In disputes, battles, riots, and civil unrest, I shall secure their victory;
I shall bestow upon them the perfection of long life.
And I shall provide protection for that realm and city;
may the Blessed One grant me permission for this.
Homage to all the Tathāgatas, to all the Bodhisattvas, and to the noble ones beginning with Avalokiteśvara and Vajrapāṇi.
Oṃ, Great Goddess, terrible one of terrifying intellect!
Victorious one, bringer of victory!
O you whose speed is fame, whose speed is splendor!

O you who have attained the prophecy [of enlightenment], who behold all sentient beings, and who abound in the splendor of compassion—protect that which is authorized by the Tathāgata! Remember your vow!
By the empowerment of the Buddha, grant me this boon!
Accomplish the success!
O Goddess, Great Goddess, Goddess of True Speech, O Bhīme, established in true speech, dweller in the secret place, svāhā!
These, O Blessed One, are those mantra-words, empowered by the Tathāgata and authorized by the Tathāgata, which have been spoken by me for the benefit of sentient beings.

Whatever desire one may have in mind, having recited [the mantra] before the Tathāgata after making offerings of flowers, incense, perfumes, and lamps, and having given an offering of milk-rice and broth in the four directions, I shall fulfill every hope through eight hundred recitations of that very [mantra]. Whoever should desire me in my own form, by him [an image should be commissioned] with a painter who has uncut fingernails, whose hair is removed, whose limbs are free from scabs, and who stands upon nine vessels on the eighth lunar day, while being sustained by the Noble Eightfold Path.

She should be painted white as a stalk of reed (*śarakāṇḍa*), her limbs adorned with all ornaments, and clad in white garments. In the center, an image of the Tathāgata should be depicted teaching the Dharma. To the right, Noble Avalokiteśvara should be shown engaged in conversation;
on the left side, the Great Goddess Bhīmā should be depicted, attended by Kuṇḍika and Netṛka, consoling [the practitioner].

Then, on the eighth day, having performed the preliminary consecration, one should offer flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, and ointments at the site of a reliquary (*caitya*) containing relics, and present offerings of meat, liquor, curd, and rice in the four directions until the full moon on the fifteenth day.

A pure Vidyādhara, having performed a most magnificent worship with flowers, incense, perfumes, and lamps, and having offered a bali-oblation consisting of various flavors and other things as they may be obtained—specifically a white bali—should, with a mind of loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings, take hold of that image with eight hundred *jāti* flowers. Reciting the mantra once for each flower, I shall appear there in my own form and grant whatever boon is desired: sovereignty over a kingdom, the power of traveling through the sky, the science of alchemy (*nidhivāda*), the science of transmutation (*dhātuvāda*), the state of a Vidyādhara, or other such powers.

And I shall perform all desired deeds: the warding off of untimely death, the pacification of all diseases, the crushing of enemy armies, the obtaining of sons, the acquisition of wealth, and affection toward all sentient beings.

O Blessed One, if I should commit the five acts of immediate retribution and yet fail to fulfill every hope, or if I should not awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—excluding those who reject the True Dharma and those who have fallen into doubt regarding the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.
The Blessed One said:

"Excellent, excellent, sister! It is indeed excellent, sister, that you have set out for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, and that you have set out so that this very Dharma discourse may endure for a long time."
"Therefore, sister, you must always keep these vows constantly in mind.
At that moment, this great earth trembled and a rain of divine flowers fell from above.
And that entire assembly gave a cry of "Excellent!"
"Excellent, excellent! This well-spoken word shall be a vow that fulfills all hopes for all sentient beings.

Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara again addressed the Blessed One: "Furthermore, Blessed One, what [merit] will that son of good family or daughter of good family obtain through writing, reciting, or causing it to be written..."
By means of proclaiming, reciting, studying, honoring, and elucidating this Dharma-discourse, one will obtain merit.
The Blessed One said:
"In that case, Noble Avalokiteśvara, I shall question you; answer as you see fit."
Avalokiteśvara said:
"May the Blessed One himself explain it; for there is nothing that the Tathāgata has not seen, has not heard, or has not known.
The Blessed One said:

And, noble son, the merit that one shall obtain from writing, causing to be written, reading, honoring, proclaiming, reciting, and studying this Dharma-discourse cannot be described even by means of a simile. Why is that?
Having given gifts that fulfill the intentions of all sentient beings, those beings remain indeed unliberated from aging, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair.

Even after being made to sport with the five strands of sensual pleasure for a thousand years, those beings remain indeed unliberated; they once again experience sufferings in the realms of hell-beings, animals, the world of Yama, and hungry ghosts.
Having caused sentient beings to hear this Dharma-discourse, having performed worship and its proclamation, and having understood its meaning, they practice it through actual application;
thus they become completely liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, and from all the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama.
Therefore, the Tathāgatas do not establish even a measure for this mass of merit by means of a simile.

And whichever noble son, for the sake of this Dharma discourse, should renounce even as much gold as a mustard seed, or a single flower, or a single fruit, or a single banner, or music, or incense, or clothing, or a seat, or an ornament; and who should write it, cause it to be written, preserve it, recite it, worship it, honor it, and extensively proclaim it to others, as well as that Dharma-preacher—

Suppose someone were to recite and worship the Tathāgata while he is present, honoring and revering him together with his assembly with every kind of offering of comfort for a hundred thousand years; suppose they were to attend upon him with perfumes, garlands, ointments, banners, and flags, and cause monasteries, walkways, and groves to be built;

and suppose they were to construct a stūpa made of the seven precious gems, half a yojana in height—whether one hundred or one thousand of them dedicated to the Tathāgata—and were to honor them with divine offerings for a hundred thousand years;
this latter person would generate a much greater accumulation of merit than the former.

By means of writing, causing to be written, upholding, reciting, honoring, and proclaiming this Dharma-discourse, one performs this worship of the Tathāgata in his presence, but not by giving gifts to sentient beings or by causing them to sport with the five strands of sensual pleasure.
Therefore, those sons of good family, daughters of good family, kings, princes, high officials, or ministers should always and constantly honor this Dharma-discourse.
One should conceive of them as Tathāgatas.
One should listen to this Dharma-discourse with reverence from those spiritual friends who cause it to be heard, who explain it, and who provide its meaning;
it should be taken up, retained, maintained, recited, and reflected upon.
One should generate the thought:
"We have gained a great gain;

we have obtained what is well-obtained—that which has been heard by us, which shows the path to those traveling on a wrong path, to those who perceive non-benefit as benefit, the impermanent as permanent, and the unpleasant as pleasant, and which serves for our liberation from the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama."
The work of the Tathāgata has been accomplished.
Avalokiteśvara said:
"By means of this great work, the work of the Tathāgata, this Dharma-discourse has been revealed for the sake of all sentient beings."
The Blessed One said:

"And this Dharma-discourse, noble son, will circulate in the southern region during the final period, in the final age. There too, monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, kings, princes, high officials, and ministers will become worthy vessels; they will be its worshippers, its upholders, and its reciters, and they will have faith and conviction in it."

If he should wander in the north, east, west, or south, those beings will be occupied with the affairs of others; they will not hear, will not have faith, will not believe, and will not honor [the teaching]. Having inferior vigor, their mindfulness lost, and possessed of various distractions—such as thoughts of family, male and female servants, enjoyments, power, laughter, dancing, acting, singing, envy, and stinginess—they will not hear, will not believe, and will not honor it; thus they remain unliberated.

Thus they shall be delivered from old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and despair, and from the realms of the hungry ghosts and the world of Yama. Therefore, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who desire to liberate themselves from all states of woe should, with reverence, honor, uphold, revere, and proclaim to others this Dharma-discourse, and should bear it in mind.

In times of riots, tumults, bad dreams, and ill omens; and in the face of untimely death, the death of cattle, the death of livestock, the death of humans, and various calamities arising from the fear of diseases—this Dharma-discourse should be honored and recited.
Or, having raised it upon a banner and honored it with various perfumes, flowers, incense, and musical instruments, one should perform rites.
Having offered oblations in the four directions and paid homage with flowers, incense, and perfumes, all such calamities will be pacified.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"Those [teachings] which were spoken by the Leaders in previous existences for the sake of favoring every sentient being,"
"I shall teach you likewise;
take up this samādhi, Ānanda. ||1||
And whoever should give gifts throughout the three realms, filling them with the seven precious jewels,
while remaining ever heedful regarding the Buddhas and the Dharmas—
Even a comparison cannot suffice for his gift. ||2||
And whoever, having placed their deep faith in the Buddhas,
should have monasteries built and shrines erected;
and whoever should uphold this sutra—
This merit will be far greater than that. ||3||
And whoever should cast down even a single flower, a garment, a garland, or likewise an ointment,
and should honor this samādhi—
The merit from this is not as great as that. ||4||
And whoever should give even a single kārṣāpaṇa coin for the sake of honoring this sūtra,
having generated a mind of loving-kindness directed toward awakening;
this person would obtain much greater merit than that. ||5||
And whatever bodhisattva should reveal this samādhi among sentient beings, teach it,
and likewise establish them in unsurpassed awakening;
There is not even a comparison nor any merit for him. ||6||
Having heard this and likewise having cultivated loving-kindness toward all sentient beings,
one should therefore uphold this sutra.
One should write it, recite it, and likewise proclaim it.
They are tormented by old age, sickness, and death, as well as by hundreds of exceedingly intense sufferings,
being reborn in the hells and among the hungry ghosts.
Lest you come to regret it in the future. ||8||
At the time of death, his mind terrified with fear,
he gasps for breath again and again;
who will be our protection and our ultimate refuge?
One of childish intellect looks from face to face. ||9||
Because, having venerated the Tathāgata,
as well as the Buddha's Dharma and the Saṅgha,
I shall seize and carry them off to the dreadful world of Yama.
For him, there will never be any protection whatsoever. ||10||
Neither son nor wife, nor friends nor kinsmen, nor even the kingdom, nor laughter and dance;
neither wealth nor grain, nor clothing and ornaments.
Having abandoned everything once more, which is harsh with suffering. ||11||
Having no faith in this samādhi,
one experiences such terrible suffering;
having heard of this suffering, [one should realize] these benefits.
What person of childish intellect would not feel devotion toward him? ||12||
Therefore, those monks, nuns,
laymen, laywomen, and kings should always uphold this sutra.
And one should always show honor to those who uphold what is to be done. ||13||
Then the venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
"I have grasped this Dharma-discourse, O Blessed One; I shall uphold it with the perception of it as the Teacher, I shall honor it, and I shall reveal it fully to all sentient beings.
The Blessed One said:
"Ānanda, if you were not to retain, recite, honor, or propagate all that Dharma which has been spoken by me and heard by you, you would not have offended me, nor would there be a failure to listen,

nor a state of non-discipleship on your part. However, whoever does not retain, recite, honor, proclaim, or attend to this Dharma-discourse— that person would offend me, a failure to listen would have occurred, and a state of non-discipleship would have ensued."
Therefore, Ānanda, you should respectfully uphold this Dharma-discourse.
In the future time, in the final age, this will perform for you the Tathāgata’s work of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment for the sake of all sentient beings.

Now, while this Dharma-discourse was being spoken by the Blessed One, the minds of sixty thousand living beings were liberated from the outflows through non-clinging, and seven hundred [beings] attained the samādhis of a bodhisattva.
Five hundred [beings] received the prophecy of their attainment of various buddha-fields.
Ninety thousand living beings were liberated from all afflictions; all unfavorable conditions, states of woe, and miserable rebirths were abandoned.
Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara again addressed the Blessed One as follows:

"Blessed One, in the future time, in the final age, this Dharma discourse will perform the work of a Tathāgata for those sons of good family who hear it, uphold it, honor it, and for those who write it down.
They have been prophesied to attain awakening in various Buddha-fields according to their aspirations."

And those beings who, in the future time, in the final age, being full of various distractions through laughter, dance, song, and instrumental music; blinded by passion, hatred, and delusion; perceiving pleasure and play in what is not pleasure; perceiving permanence in what is impermanent;
seized by envy, stinginess, and immorality; will neither worship, nor honor, nor have faith in, nor believe in, nor uphold, nor hear, nor practice according to the teaching.
Having exhausted that store of the auspicious fruits of their former karma, they will experience the various sufferings and mental distresses of hellish pain.
Then, after experiencing suffering for many hundreds of millions of eons, they will be reborn in the hells, the animal realm, or the world of Yama.
Having squandered this present moment, they will long endure under the influence of evil friends and will later be filled with remorse.
Therefore, one should indeed practice restraint of body, speech, and mind;

one should possess unshakable faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha; one should maintain a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings, being completely free from envy, stinginess, and immoral thoughts, and being free from anger.
Then, that assembled assembly, through those various accumulations of merit, honored the Tathāgata.

With divine flowers, perfumes, garlands, ointments, garments, and ornaments, and with shouts of "kilikili" and "prakṣveḍita," and with the music of divine instruments, drums, and cymbals, he offered his approval, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Blessed One! This great Dharma discourse is well-spoken for the benefit of all sentient beings and for the long endurance of the Tathāgata’s teaching.
Then the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, what is the name of this Dharma-discourse, and how, Blessed One, should we remember it?
The Blessed One said:
"Therefore, Ānanda, you should remember this Dharma-discourse by the name 'The Progression through the Bodhisattva Stages of the Wisdom of All Tathāgatas.'"
"Remember it also by the name 'The Great Assembly of the Noble Ones Displaying Miraculous Powers.
Remember it also by the name 'The Array that Manifests Buddha-fields through the Blessing of All Tathāgatas and the Surveying of Sentient Beings.
Thus spoke the Blessed One."

With uplifted minds, all the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, headed by Āryāvalokiteśvara, Mañjuśrī, and Vajrapāṇi; all the great Śrāvakas; all the Śakras, Brahmās, and World-Protectors; the four Great Kings; the great Yakṣiṇīs, beginning with Anaupamyā, Vimalaprabhā, Prabhāvatī, Bhīmā, Śrī, Śaṅkhinī, Haritā, and Mahādevī; and the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas—this entire assembly, having gathered together, rejoiced at what the Blessed One had spoken and gave their approval, saying, "Excellent!"
"Excellent, excellent, Blessed One!
[Thus ends the Mahāyāna Sūtra titled "The Array of the Manifestation of Buddha-fields through the Beholding of Beings by the Empowerment of All Tathāgatas."]
